result:
The proposed answer of 1 is almost certainly wrong.

The question asks for a ratio as a function of $r$, which suggests the multiplicity grows with the level exponent. The proposed argument also has a specific gap. It claims the $\alpha$-eigenspace of $U_\wp$ in $\pi_\wp^{K_1(\wp^r)}$ is one-dimensional for all $r\ge 1$. For unramified principal series, which is the local type of finite-slope eigensystems that are $\wp$-old from level $\mathfrak{n}\wp$, the dimension of the $K_1(\wp^r)$-fixed space grows with $r$ (Casselman-type computations). Only the generic-newform/Steinberg case stays one-dimensional, and that case does not fit the finite-slope eigensystems here. Inclusion $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp))\subset S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp^r))$ gives only a lower bound, not equality of multiplicities.

I have not verified the exact formula from the literature. My recollection is that the multiplicity at level $\mathfrak{n}\wp^r$ is $r$ times the multiplicity at level $\mathfrak{n}\wp$, which would make the ratio $r$, but I cannot confirm that here. What matters for this verdict is that the proposed constant answer does not survive the local representation-theoretic analysis.

VERDICT: REJECT

CONFIDENCE: 4
